model: Offline change-point detection (ruptures: PELT, Binseg, KernelCPD)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Dates of structural breaks in class fill and in flow series (August layout change, allocation-rule tweaks, consolidation days), used to set the training window.
inputs_needed: Historical daily series (fill, inflow, outflow per class).
library: ruptures (Pelt, Binseg, BottomUp, Window, Dynp, KernelCPD; costs L1/L2/Normal/Rbf/AR)
strengths: Objective evidence for which history is comparable. Cheap.
weaknesses: Offline only. Penalty choice drives the number of breaks.
evidence: ruptures docs; Truong, Oudre & Vayatis 2020 review (Signal Processing).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fill ratio per cell class at d+1..d+14 equals today's snapshot value.
inputs_needed: Daily 06:00 occupancy snapshot per class.
strengths: Very hard to beat at 24-48 h, because occupancy is a stock that changes slowly. It is the mandatory reference for skill scores.
weaknesses: Blind to planned inflows and outflows, month-end build-up and shipment waves. Any intervals come from residual quantiles only.
evidence: In fev-bench, Seasonal Naive is the floor (about 20% win rate), yet persistence of stocks is typically strong at short horizons.

model: Seasonal naive (weekly, lag 7 calendar days or 5 working days)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fill per class at d+h equals the value on the same weekday last week.
inputs_needed: At least 1-2 weeks of daily snapshots, plus a working-day calendar.
strengths: Captures the weekday pattern of production and shipping (weekend troughs, Friday shipments).
weaknesses: Worse than persistence when the level is drifting. Ignores plans.
evidence: Standard benchmark in fev-bench and the M5 competition.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: AutoML ensemble of statistical, tabular and Chronos models with quantile forecasts per class.
inputs_needed: TimeSeriesDataFrame plus known_covariates_names (plans, calendar); other columns are treated as past covariates.
strengths: The easiest route to Chronos-2 with known-future covariates, LoRA or full fine-tuning, and a weighted ensemble. Reports covariate feature importance.
weaknesses: Black-box ensemble. Fine-tuning on ~70 points is risky. Chronos-Bolt only gets covariates via an external regressor (per-timestep effects only).
evidence: AutoGluon tutorial: on electricity load, Chronos-2 with covariates scored MASE 0.696 vs 1.278 for univariate Chronos-Bolt-small. Fine-tuning improved it only to 0.688.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Single API for the whole ladder: naive, ARIMA, regression models, deep models, Chronos2Model, conformal wrappers, ensembles, historical_forecasts backtests.
inputs_needed: TimeSeries objects for target, past_covariates and future_covariates.
strengths: Explicit past vs future covariate semantics, which suit plans. Chronos2Model supports past and future covariates. ConformalNaiveModel and ConformalQRModel wrap any model. Built-in rolling backtest.
weaknesses: In Darts, TimesFM2p5Model and TiRexModel have no covariate support. Wrapper overhead.
evidence: Darts README model table (fetched Oct 2026).

model: Additive advanced pickup model for not-yet-notified shipments
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Outbound pallets beyond the 24-72 h notice horizon = notified pallets on hand + expected additional notices still to arrive ('pickup'), from historical notice curves by lead time, weekday and month-end.
inputs_needed: Timestamped shipment notices (creation time and ship date) and realised shipments.
min_history: 6-12 weeks (carpark/hotel studies used rolling windows of a few weeks to 12 weeks).
strengths: Turns the booking curve of shipment notices into the outbound term of the flow balance for days 3-14.
weaknesses: Needs notice creation timestamps, which may not be stored historically.
evidence: Weatherford & Kimes (2003): exponential smoothing and pickup most robust for hotel arrivals, pickup lowest MAPE. Papayiannis et al. (2016): additive beat multiplicative, advanced slightly beat classical; best 7-day model Add-Advan-HW. Wickham (1995): pickup models beat time series and regression for airline demand under 8 weeks, advanced pickup best.

model: Allocation-cascade router (smallest fitting class first, spill to larger classes, reserved wide cells)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Which cell class each forecast inbound pallet lands in, how much spills into larger classes, and how many pallets find no compatible free cell (sent to the floor buffer).
inputs_needed: Load-unit dimension -> feasible cell-class matrix; WMS priority order; reservation rule for W1000 cells (to be reverse-engineered from snapshots such as 20 May 2026); weekly material caps; defrag trigger threshold and weekly mission rate.
min_history: Rule-based. Validate on a few weeks of consecutive snapshot pairs (day t -> t+1).
strengths: Reproduces the non-linear effect of Medium 800 being full while total fill is only 84%, which aggregate time-series models cannot see. Produces the 'no compatible cell' KPI directly. Siemens Plant Simulation's high-bay-warehouse WMS object uses the same two assignment modes (by pallet dimension and by preallocation table), so this is a standard WMS pattern.
weaknesses: The hidden 'allocation system' rule must be inferred from data. Any gap between modelled and real WMS decisions becomes class-level bias. Defrag timing is discretionary.
evidence: Cardona & Gue (2019) define the service level of a rack with several slot heights as the probability that all pallets present can be stored, and report 29-45% space savings from multi-height slots, showing that class-level feasibility rather than total fill is the binding quantity.

model: Flow-balance occupancy simulator per cell class (deterministic core)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Occupied and free cells per cell class for each day 1-14 ahead: 06:00 snapshot + planned inbound pallets (moulding/assembly output, purchase receipts, returning empty containers) - planned outbound pallets (shipments, assembly consumption, emptied pallboxes).
inputs_needed: Daily 06:00 snapshot by cell class and load-unit type; SAP/MES production plan converted pieces->pallets via packing spec; purchase-order schedule; shipment notices; assembly consumption plan (BOM); load-unit->cell-class fit table; weekly AW entry caps.
min_history: None to run; about 4-8 weeks of snapshots plus movements to calibrate pieces->pallets factors and to backtest.
compute: Seconds per 14-day run on a laptop.
strengths: Uses the strongest signal available (plans known to the hour, ~90% of the 10-day plan realised). Every forecast pallet is traceable, works with only the few months of post-August-2026 history, and is the natural base for what-if.
weaknesses: Misses unplanned flows (QC holds, partial pallbox returns, defrag, floor-buffer re-entries). Sensitive to wrong pieces->pallets conversion. Deterministic unless wrapped in Monte Carlo.
evidence: Same structure as hospital census models that sum patients still present plus scheduled admissions times probability of still being in bed (van den Broek d'Obrenan et al. 2020; Isken & Littig 2007), and as container-yard inventory driven by weekly vessel schedules and dwell times (Kim & Youn 2013).
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. Cited sources exist and match: van den Broek d'Obrenan et al. 2020 split occupancy into present patients plus scheduled patients times probability still in bed; Isken & Littig 2007; Kim & Youn 2013 yard inventory vs weekly schedules and dwell times.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot 21-quantile forecasts of all 5 class fill series jointly (group attention), conditioned on known-future plans and calendar and on past-only covariates (e.g. defrag missions, floor-buffer count).
inputs_needed: Context df (id, timestamp, target, covariates) plus future_df with known covariates.
library: chronos-forecasting Chronos2Pipeline.predict_df; autogluon presets chronos2 / chronos2_small; darts Chronos2Model
compute: 120M (small 28M); CPU feasible for 5 series; context up to 8192, prediction up to 1024
strengths: Native past-only, known-future and categorical covariates. Multivariate in-context learning across classes. Best overall in fev-bench. LoRA or full fine-tuning available through AutoGluon.
weaknesses: Black box. No hard capacity constraint, so quantiles can exceed 100%. No static covariates in Darts. In-context covariate effects are only as good as about 70 days of context allow. Fine-tuning on short series can hurt (break-even paper).
evidence: fev-bench: probabilistic win rate 91.4%, point 87.2% (1st of 100 tasks). Paper: outperforms baselines on covariate tasks 'by a wide margin'. About 300 series/s on an A10G GPU.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot regression of class fill on time features plus known-future plan covariates, with quantile output.
inputs_needed: context_df plus future_df with known covariates (plans, calendar).
library: tabpfn-time-series (TabPFNTSPipeline.predict_df); CLIENT (cloud API) or LOCAL mode
license: Repo Apache-2.0; LOCAL checkpoint needs acceptance of the Prior Labs license
compute: CLIENT: no GPU (cloud); LOCAL: GPU recommended
strengths: Tabular foundation model, so it maps plan features to fill with tiny data. Strong on small tabular-style problems. Defaults moved to TabPFN-3.5 (Sep 2026).
weaknesses: Past dynamic and static covariates are dropped. Multivariate is split into univariate series. CLIENT mode sends data to the cloud and telemetry is on by default. Slow (median 305 s per task in the Chronos-2 paper table).
evidence: fev-bench probabilistic win rate 69.7%. Only TabPFN models consistently beat EPF benchmarks in three markets (Lipiecki & Weron 2026). Competitive zero-shot on TSO load (Hertel et al. 2026).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Corrected occupancy per class = simulator forecast + ML-predicted residual capturing systematic bias from unplanned moves, defrag, QC holds and plan non-realisation.
inputs_needed: Archived simulator forecasts and realised occupancy by origin and horizon; calendar features; plan-change indicators; floor-buffer level.
min_history: A backlog of forecast-vs-actual pairs: re-run the simulator on archived snapshots to create 2-3 months of pseudo-history.
strengths: Keeps mechanistic structure while learning what the plan misses. Quantile or conformal wrappers give calibrated bands.
weaknesses: Needs enough origins for learning; residuals shift when WMS rules change.
evidence: Hanisch et al. (2005) correct a synchronised online simulation against measured totals and note there is no general correction rule. Ordu et al. (2021) chain forecasting -> DES -> MILP for hospital resources. Wikman-Jorgensen et al. (2022) combined a Markov admissions generator with DES and reached bed-occupancy errors of about 5% of beds at a weekly horizon.

model: Existing-stock depletion via residual dwell-time survival and Poisson-binomial census
what_it_predicts_for_coster: For every pallet in today's snapshot without a firm exit plan, P(still stored on day d) from its age and the conditional survival curve. Summing these Bernoullis gives an exact Poisson-binomial distribution of residual stock per class.
inputs_needed: Snapshot with entry timestamp per pallet, material and load-unit type, survival curves by group, and optionally an ERP/planner expected exit date per pallet.
min_history: Entry/exit timestamps of completed stays; censoring handles pallets still stored.
library: lifelines or scikit-survival + numpy (Poisson-binomial by DP/FFT)
strengths: Explicitly models the largest block of tomorrow's occupancy (today's stock). Combines planner exit dates with statistical curves, as hospitals combine physician discharge estimates with LOS data.
weaknesses: Assumes pallets leave independently, but shipments are batched (e.g., 70 pallet boxes per container). Needs reliable entry timestamps from the WLog movement log.
evidence: Bos et al. (2025, Omega) combine physicians' estimated discharge dates with LOS distributions using the Poisson binomial distribution and probabilistic convolution to give full bed-census distributions. Bekker, uit het Broek & Koole (2023) predict occupancy by fitting residual lengths of stay and applying queueing theory.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Non-parametric distribution of time-in-AW per material group, load-unit type and flow (finished goods, semi-finished, purchased, empty containers), handling right-censoring of pallets still stored.
inputs_needed: Entry and exit timestamps per pallet from WLog movements; group labels.
min_history: A few hundred completed stays per group. Dwell time is a material property, so pre-August-2026 history may still be usable.
strengths: Simple and censoring-correct. Plugs directly into the M_t/G/inf and residual-stock models. Likely more stable across the layout change than occupancy itself.
weaknesses: No covariates. Thin groups give noisy curves. Month-end build-up needs stratification.
evidence: Baas et al. (2021) used Kaplan-Meier LOS estimates as a core input of an occupancy forecaster that hospitals adopted in capacity dashboards. lifelines is a pure-Python survival package with Kaplan-Meier, Nelson-Aalen and regression (MIT licence).

model: LightGBM with lag and plan features (direct multi-horizon, global over classes)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Residual of the flow-balance simulator (or fill change) per class and horizon, from lags, plan features, plan-slip proxies and calendar.
inputs_needed: Snapshots, simulator output, plan covariates (known future), calendar, class id.
min_history: ~a few hundred rows (pooled classes x horizons); with ~70 days keep trees tiny
library: lightgbm; mlforecast MLForecast (X_df); skforecast ForecasterDirect; darts LightGBMModel(output_chunk_length=14)
strengths: Proven workhorse for tabular forecasting with exogenous drivers. Non-linear interactions (fill x planned inflow near capacity). Quantile objective or conformal for intervals.
weaknesses: Overfits on ~70 daily points. Needs strong regularisation (num_leaves 4-8, min_data_in_leaf, monotone constraints on planned inflow). Cannot extrapolate beyond levels seen in training.
evidence: M5: 4 of the top 5 used LightGBM, all top-50 methods used cross-learning, and the winner was 22.4% better than the best benchmark.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Global GBM or linear models over the 5 classes with lag transforms and dynamic plan features.
inputs_needed: df plus static features plus X_df with future dynamic exog.
strengths: Handles lags, rolling features and static and dynamic exog. Conformal intervals calibrated separately per horizon step.
weaknesses: Few calibration windows with a short history, so the interval quantiles are coarse.
evidence: MLForecast docs: dynamic exog via X_df. Conformal intervals adjusted per horizon step (Stankeviciute et al. 2021).

model: Ridge / linear regression with lag and plan features (direct multi-horizon, global)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fill (or change in fill) per class at each horizon h=1..14 from current fill, recent changes, cumulative planned net inflow up to h, weekday and month-end flags.
inputs_needed: Snapshots plus plan features, pooled across 5 classes (class as a categorical or one-hot).
strengths: The most data-efficient learned model. Coefficients are readable. Direct per-horizon models avoid feeding errors back recursively. Supports quantile output in Darts and conformal intervals in skforecast and MLForecast.
weaknesses: Linear, so it misses the saturation and cascade non-linearity near 100%.
evidence: Darts table: LinearRegressionModel supports past, future and static covariates, multi-series and probabilistic output.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Scikit-learn and LightGBM forecasters (recursive, direct, multi-series, classifier, foundation) with exog and probabilistic intervals.
inputs_needed: pandas series plus exog DataFrame with future rows.
strengths: Fits the team's sklearn/LightGBM stack. Bootstrapped-residual, conformal and quantile intervals with CRPS and coverage metrics. Backtesting with gaps and refits.
weaknesses: Multi-output direct models multiply parameters by 14 horizons.
evidence: skforecast docs v0.26.0.

model: Monte Carlo plan-slip ensemble around the flow balance
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Distribution of occupancy per class per day, P(fill > 80%) and P(fill > 90%), expected pallets without a compatible cell, and time-to-full quantiles for the 40-48 h email alert.
inputs_needed: Flow balance + cascade inputs plus empirical error distributions: plan realisation (~90% over 10 days), timing slips, quantity deviations, shipment-notice lead times (FCA 48 h, DAP 24 h, containers 48-72 h), dwell-time survival for stock without planned exit, QC-hold probability.
min_history: About 2-3 months of plan-vs-actual pairs. Plan versions must be archived daily from now on.
compute: 1,000 runs x 14 days: seconds to about a minute on a laptop.
strengths: Turns the deterministic simulator into threshold-crossing probabilities, which is exactly the alert output. Scenarios and what-if come almost free.
weaknesses: Only as good as the slip distributions. Correlated slips (one press stop delays several orders; 70-pallet containers) must be modelled or bands will be too narrow. Needs stored plan snapshots.
evidence: Baas et al. (2021) simulated 1,000 Monte Carlo trajectories from admission forecasts and Kaplan-Meier LOS; ICU 95% intervals covered realised occupancy in 74-97% of cases, with lower ward coverage attributed to unmodelled parameter uncertainty. Witteborg et al. (2022) fed patient-level LOS distributions and planned admissions into Monte Carlo; a simple policy on the resulting probabilities would have avoided critical ICU occupancy in about 70% of cases.

model: Nested cell-class feasibility / max-flow capacity check
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Minimum possible number of pallets without a compatible free cell for the forecast load-unit mix (pallet -> any cell with enough height and width), compared with WMS-realised placements to separate policy-induced overflow from true lack of space.
inputs_needed: Forecast pallet counts by load-unit type per day; cell-class counts; fit matrix.
strengths: Exact and tiny. Gives the upper bound of storable pallets and quantifies the cost of the wide-cell reserve rule and the value of defrag.
weaknesses: Ignores sequencing (pallets parked in big cells until defrag), so it is a bound, not a forecast.
evidence: Cardona & Gue (2019) use 'probability that all pallets present can be stored' as the service level for racks with several slot heights; Cardona's dissertation (2019) also addresses storage shortages under multiple slot heights.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Online-adjusted interval level alpha_t per class and horizon that widens after misses and narrows after hits.
inputs_needed: Stream of forecasts and realised fills.
library: mapie TimeSeriesRegressor(method='aci', gamma); custom few-line implementation
strengths: Long-run coverage under arbitrary distribution shift. Suits post-layout and WMS-rule regime changes.
weaknesses: Can produce infinite intervals after a run of misses. Gamma needs tuning. Coverage holds only on average over time.
evidence: Gibbs & Candès, NeurIPS 2021. MAPIE docs describe the aci method and its infinite-set behaviour.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Simulated fill trajectories (resampled backtest residuals added to point paths), giving P(max fill over the next 48 h >= 90%) and the expected number of days above 80%.
inputs_needed: Point model plus pool of in-sample or backtest residuals per horizon.
strengths: The only wrapper here that yields joint paths, so it gives the probability of crossing a threshold within a window (not just per-day marginals). Combines with Monte Carlo plan slips in rung 2.
weaknesses: Ignores the dependence structure unless block bootstrap is used. Inherits bias from the point model.
evidence: skforecast docs: bootstrapped-residual intervals with CRPS and coverage metrics.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Recalibrates quantile-model bands (LightGBM quantile, QRF, Chronos-2 quantiles) to the target coverage.
inputs_needed: Quantile forecasts plus a calibration set of outcomes.
strengths: Keeps adaptive, heteroscedastic widths while fixing miscalibration. A natural way to calibrate foundation-model quantiles.
weaknesses: Assumes exchangeability (pair with ACI for drift).
evidence: Romano, Patterson & Candès 2019: shorter intervals than other conformal approaches.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Conformal intervals for sklearn-style regressors, including time-series EnbPI and ACI.
inputs_needed: sklearn estimator plus X, y.
strengths: Already in the team's planned stack. Simple update loop for live alerts.
weaknesses: TimeSeriesRegressor is single-output. API changed in v1.x. No path-wise (within-48 h) crossing probability.
evidence: MAPIE 1.2.1 docs.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Interval for fill at each horizon h from the empirical quantile of rolling-origin backtest errors at that h. Can be wrapped around any rung.
inputs_needed: Rolling-origin backtest residuals per class and horizon.
library: mlforecast PredictionIntervals(n_windows,h); statsforecast ConformalIntervals; sktime ConformalIntervals(method='conformal'/'conformal_bonferroni'); darts ConformalNaiveModel
strengths: Model-agnostic. Calibrated per horizon. Simplest valid-ish intervals for any rung.
weaknesses: Assumes errors are exchangeable across windows, which a regime change breaks. With 20 calibration points, the 90% quantile is roughly the 2nd-largest error.
evidence: Sabashvili 2026: multi-step split conformal met 90% coverage with the best efficiency (AutoARIMA base). Stankeviciute et al. 2021 give multi-horizon guarantees.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Expected pallets in the AW per class from each flow stream: m(t) = integral of lambda(u) * P(S > t-u) du (arrival rate convolved with the dwell-time survival function). With Poisson arrivals the count is Poisson, so P(occupancy > threshold) follows in closed form.
inputs_needed: Inbound rate per day by flow type (planned or forecast), dwell-time survival function per flow type, residual survival of existing stock.
min_history: Enough completed stays to fit survival curves per flow group (a few hundred pallets per group).
strengths: Closed form. Explains why occupancy peaks lag inbound peaks. Gives a distribution without simulation. Ideal for flows without an explicit outbound plan (empty metal containers, partial pallboxes, QC quarantine).
weaknesses: Infinite capacity ignores blocking, overflow and the cascade. Poisson variance is too small for batch arrivals from production runs. Needs a capacity correction near 100%.
evidence: Eick, Massey & Whitt (1993) show the M_t/G/inf mean is a linear operator applied to the arrival rate, the count is Poisson under suitable initial conditions, and peak congestion lags the peak arrival rate. Baas et al. (2021) ran a network of such queues operationally in Dutch hospitals. Akbari-Moghaddam et al. (2025) show static 85% occupancy rules fail where M_t/G_t/inf captures daily exceedances.

model: Online (look-ahead) simulation initialised from the current state
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Nightly or 06:00 transient run of the flow-balance/DES model starting from the live snapshot, projecting occupancy per class for 7-14 days with traffic-light flags per day and class.
inputs_needed: Live snapshot (positions, holds, quarantine), plans, equipment status; automated data extraction and validation checks.
min_history: None to run; about 3 months of daily runs to validate.
strengths: Proven pattern for short-horizon industrial forecasting. No warm-up because the model starts from the true state. A 'last 3 days forecast vs actual' strip builds user trust.
weaknesses: Highly sensitive to snapshot data quality, so automated validation checks are needed. Unmeasured state (e.g., pallets in transit) must be estimated.
evidence: Infineon: daily 7-day WIP forecast from current lot and equipment state reached >90% aggregated accuracy within three months (Seidel et al. 2017); 35-day short-term model >90% (Mosinski et al. 2017); green/yellow/red display with last 3 days of history (Scholl et al. 2023). Cardin & Castagna (2011) and Hanisch et al. (2005) describe DES as a short-term forecasting tool started from the actual state; Gunn & Nahavandi (2002) show that omitting initial WIP gives wrong results.

model: ARIMA / SARIMAX / dynamic regression with exogenous plan variables
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Daily change in fill per class regressed on planned net inflow (planned in minus planned out, in pallets per class), weekday and month-end dummies, with ARIMA errors.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots plus future plan series (moulding and assembly output, shipments, PO receipts) mapped to load-unit and cell class.
library: statsmodels SARIMAX; statsforecast AutoARIMA (X_df); darts ARIMA/AutoARIMA (future_covariates)
strengths: This is the statistical twin of the flow-balance simulator. The coefficient on planned net flow shows how much of the plan materialises, and the ARIMA errors absorb slips and unplanned moves. Interpretable for plant staff.
weaknesses: Needs future values of every regressor. Intervals are conditional on the plan and ignore plan uncertainty (fpp3). Linear, so it cannot represent the saturation and cascade at 100%.
evidence: In M5, ARIMAX was about 13% more accurate than plain ARIMA and ESX about 6% better than ES, and every winning entry used external information (M5 paper).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fast fitting of naive, ETS, ARIMA(X), Theta, CES, MFLES and Croston for the 5 classes, with intervals.
inputs_needed: Long-format df (unique_id, ds, y, exog...) plus X_df for future exog.
library: statsforecast (StatsForecast, AutoARIMA, AutoETS, AutoTheta, Naive, SeasonalNaive; ConformalIntervals)
strengths: One API for rung 1 and the statistical challengers. Both level= intervals and conformal prediction_intervals.
weaknesses: Exogenous support varies by model (AutoTBATS ignores X, RandomWalkWithDrift takes only y).
evidence: StatsForecast docs: AutoARIMA with exogenous regressors via X_df, and level intervals.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. StatsForecast docs confirm X_df future exog with AutoARIMA, level= intervals, ConformalIntervals, AutoTBATS ignoring X and RandomWalkWithDrift fit on y only.

model: Structural time series / Kalman: local level + regression (UnobservedComponents)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Latent fill level per class driven by planned net flow, with a time-varying regression coefficient (plan realisation rate) and Gaussian predictive bands.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots (gaps allowed), planned net inflow per class, weekday dummies.
library: statsmodels UnobservedComponents(level='local level', exog=..., mle_regression=False for time-varying betas)
strengths: Fits well with a short history and a regime break: the local level re-anchors after the August layout change. The Kalman filter handles missing snapshots. A time-varying beta tracks whether only part of the plan lands. Analytic P(fill>=0.8/0.9).
weaknesses: Linear Gaussian model, so the bands do not respect the 0-100% bounds. The cascade between classes is not modelled unless a multivariate state space is built.
evidence: statsmodels docs: exog regressors, recursive time-varying coefficients when mle_regression=False (Durbin & Koopman 2012).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Live run-length posterior on forecast residuals per class, flagging regime shifts so models are retrained or ACI is reset.
inputs_needed: Stream of residuals or fill changes.
library: custom implementation (Adams & MacKay message passing); several open-source ports
strengths: Exact online algorithm with a probabilistic change signal.
weaknesses: Hazard rate and prior choices matter. A univariate model per series.
evidence: Adams & MacKay 2007.

model: Warehouse / AS-RS digital twin synchronised with WMS data
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Continuously updated replica of the AW that can simulate the near future to anticipate saturation and replay history to explain past events.
inputs_needed: WMS/WCS events, equipment states, ERP data, data-driven model tables.
min_history: Months of integration work; validation campaign.
strengths: Unifies forecasting, what-if and explanation. Frameworks and validation methods exist.
weaknesses: Interoperability and data collection across heterogeneous equipment are the main open problems. Overkill before rung 2 is proven.
evidence: Kuhl et al. (2022) present a four-part warehouse digital-twin framework that simulates the near-term future to predict problems. Ferrari et al. (2024) validate an AS/RS DES model including WMS/WCS layers through a design-of-experiments campaign in a lab.

model: Forecast combination (median or weighted ensemble of stats + ML + foundation model)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Combined quantile forecast of class fill from rung-2, rung-3 and rung-4 members, with weights learned in backtest.
inputs_needed: Member forecasts from rolling backtest.
min_history: ~30+ backtest origins for weights (else equal weights)
library: autogluon WeightedEnsemble; darts NaiveEnsembleModel / RegressionEnsembleModel; simple quantile averaging
strengths: Combining is robust to any one model failing after a regime change.
weaknesses: Harder to explain to operators. Learned weights overfit with few backtest origins.
evidence: M5: the winner averaged 6 models, the runner-up 5, and the 3rd place 43 neural networks (M5 paper).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Unified forecasting interface with ConformalIntervals wrapper and foundation-model wrappers.
inputs_needed: y, X, fh.
library: sktime (ConformalIntervals: empirical, empirical_residual, conformal, conformal_bonferroni; ChronosForecaster)
strengths: ConformalIntervals implements Stankeviciute et al. with or without a Bonferroni correction across horizons, around any point forecaster.
weaknesses: API is heavier than Nixtla or Darts for this use case.
evidence: sktime docs: ConformalIntervals methods; site: BSD-3, Chronos wrapper.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate quantile forecast (9 quantiles) per class. Strong at short horizons.
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Small xLSTM model, the best univariate zero-shot model in its paper. 2nd in fev-bench.
weaknesses: Univariate only, so plans cannot be used. Covariates were listed as future work.
evidence: fev-bench probabilistic win rate 83.3%. GIFT-Eval zero-shot CRPS 0.411 vs 0.459 next best (paper).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot multivariate streaming forecast with past and future-known covariates.
inputs_needed: Context series plus covariates.
strengths: New (Jul 2026) small covariate-aware model, streaming at constant per-patch cost.
weaknesses: Very new. License and tooling not verified. Benchmarks are self-reported.
evidence: arXiv 2607.01204: top zero-shot results on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, supports past and future-known covariates.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot quantile forecast per class. Covariates enter through XReg: a linear model on covariates, with TimesFM forecasting the residual.
inputs_needed: Context series plus dynamic numerical/categorical and static covariates covering context and horizon.
library: timesfm (2.5 code under src/timesfm; forecast with covariates via XReg); darts TimesFM2p5Model (no covariates)
compute: 200M params; context up to 16k; optional 30M quantile head
strengths: Strong univariate zero-shot accuracy with commercially usable weights.
weaknesses: XReg is linear and cannot use past-only covariates. The covariate path was missing at launch and restored on 29 Oct 2025.
evidence: fev-bench: probabilistic win rate 79.6%, point 76.1%. TimesFM GitHub news: XReg support added back for 2.5 on 29 Oct 2025.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot multivariate forecast of the 5 classes with past-only and past-future (known plan) covariates, 9 quantiles.
inputs_needed: Context series plus covariates.
license: Code Apache-2.0; 3.0 weights under timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0 (commercial use only via Google Cloud, e.g. BigQuery ML)
strengths: Native multivariate and covariate support. Google reports it as the top pretrained model on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME (Aug 2026).
weaknesses: Self-hosted weights are non-commercial, so production at Coster would need BigQuery. Vendor-reported benchmarks.
evidence: Google Research blog, 31 Aug 2026; GitHub license notes.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot multivariate 21-quantile forecast with past-only, known-future and categorical covariates.
inputs_needed: Context target plus past_covariates and known_covariates covering context and horizon.
compute: 5M / 28M / 123M / 209M params; CPU inference; context up to 32,768
strengths: Covariate-native, small and CPU-friendly. Mistral reports the 209M model ranks 1st among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench, and the 28M model beats Chronos-2 on GIFT-Eval and TIME.
weaknesses: Released 15 Oct 2026. Vendor claims only, not independently replicated. Ecosystem immature.
evidence: Mistral announcement, 15 Oct 2026; GitHub README.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Total AW fill and free cells as the sum of class forecasts (and of class sample paths).
inputs_needed: Class-level forecasts.
strengths: Trivial and consistent. Summing joint sample paths keeps the dependence.
weaknesses: Errors add up. Ignores information in the total series.
evidence: HierarchicalForecast README.

model: Cox proportional-hazards / Weibull AFT dwell-time regression
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Dwell time conditional on covariates such as material, customer, incoterm, load-unit type, entry weekday, days to month-end, and whether a shipment notice exists.
inputs_needed: As Kaplan-Meier plus covariates from SAP/WLog.
strengths: Pools information across thin material groups. Hazard ratios make month-end and incoterm effects explicit.
weaknesses: Proportional-hazards assumption may fail. Parametric forms may misfit multimodal dwell (consumed in days vs. safety stock for months).
evidence: Poelsterl (2020, JMLR) documents penalized Cox models in scikit-survival (GPL-3). lifelines (MIT) implements CoxPHFitter and WeibullAFTFitter (Survival Regression docs).
check_note: Independent check: corrected. JMLR abstract confirms scikit-survival penalized Cox under GPL-3; lifelines is MIT (GitHub) and its docs show CoxPHFitter and WeibullAFTFitter, so the Weibull AFT caveat can be resolved.

model: Markov chain for load-unit and cell states
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Daily transitions of pallboxes between states (full in AW -> at assembly -> partial back in AW -> empty -> returned or consolidated) and of empty metal containers, giving expected cells held by partial and empty units.
inputs_needed: Daily state counts or movement events; transition frequencies per week; assembly plan as driver of picking transitions.
strengths: Captures the ~130 partial-pallbox cycles per week and empty-container returns that plans do not show. Small-data friendly.
weaknesses: Memoryless assumption. Full joint slot-state chains explode (2^m states), so aggregation is needed.
evidence: Yamashita, Ohtani & Suzuki (1998) model AS/RS slot occupancy as a Markov chain with Poisson retrievals and batch replenishment, and use exact aggregation to cut 2^m states to O(m^2) per slot.

model: CatBoost with lag and plan features
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Residual or fill change per class and horizon. Native categorical handling (class, weekday, incoterm mix).
inputs_needed: Same as LightGBM.
strengths: Ordered boosting and native categoricals are fairly robust on small data. Darts supports probabilistic CatBoost.
weaknesses: Weak probabilistic accuracy in fev-bench. Slower than LightGBM.
evidence: fev-bench: CatBoost point win rate 52.4% (above Stat. Ensemble 47.7% and TFT 45.7%) but probabilistic win rate only 34.4%.

model: Direct threshold-exceedance classifier (logistic regression or GBM binary)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: P(class fill >= 80% or >= 90% at any time within the next 48 h), a calibrated probability for the alert email.
inputs_needed: Features as in rung 3 plus label = max fill over [t, t+48h] >= threshold.
min_history: needs dozens of positive events; few months may have only a handful
library: sklearn LogisticRegression + CalibratedClassifierCV; lightgbm objective='binary'; skforecast ForecasterRecursiveClassifier
strengths: Optimises exactly the alert decision. Brier score, reliability diagrams and a cost-weighted cut-off are straightforward.
weaknesses: Positives are rare and there is no logged saturation history. Labels from 06:00 snapshots miss intra-day peaks. Probabilities taken from good quantile or sample forecasts are often better on small data. Use it as a cross-check.
evidence: LightGBM docs (binary objective). skforecast ships a recursive classifier forecaster. CORP reliability diagrams (Dimitriadis et al. 2021) for calibration checks.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Directly predicts the q-th quantile (e.g. q10/q50/q90/q95) of class fill at 48 h from plan and lag features.
inputs_needed: Snapshots plus plan features.
library: sklearn.linear_model.QuantileRegressor (pinball loss, L1 alpha, solver='highs'); statsmodels QuantReg
strengths: Interpretable tail model: 'with 300 planned pallets in, the q90 of Medium fill rises by x'. Robust to outliers. Pairs with CQR for coverage.
weaknesses: Separate fit per quantile, so quantiles can cross. Linear. Few tail observations in a short history.
evidence: scikit-learn docs (pinball loss, L1 penalty).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Full predictive distribution (e.g. Normal) of class fill at each horizon, so P(fill>=0.8/0.9) comes out in closed form.
inputs_needed: Tabular lag and plan features.
strengths: Distributional output with any base learner and scoring rule. Threshold probabilities come straight from the distribution.
weaknesses: A parametric family is mis-specified for a bounded fill ratio (use a logit transform). Less mature tooling for time series.
evidence: Duan et al. 2019: matches or exceeds existing probabilistic regression methods.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Conditional quantiles of class fill or residual per horizon.
inputs_needed: Same as LightGBM.
strengths: Non-linear, heteroscedastic intervals (wider when near capacity or before month-end).
weaknesses: One model per quantile, with crossing. Tails are poorly estimated on small data, so it needs a conformal correction (CQR).
evidence: LightGBM docs: 'quantile' objective with alpha. M5 uncertainty competition used 9 quantiles scored with pinball loss.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Non-parametric conditional distribution of fill or residual per horizon.
inputs_needed: Tabular lag and plan features.
strengths: One fit gives all quantiles. Out-of-bag estimates help on small data. Used as the residual-quantile learner in SPCI.
weaknesses: Cannot predict beyond fill levels observed in training, which matters for new highs. Coarse tails with little data.
evidence: quantile-forest README (Meinshausen 2006, JMLR).

model: XGBoost with lag and plan features
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Same target as LightGBM (residual or fill change per class and horizon).
inputs_needed: Same as LightGBM.
strengths: Mature. Quantile and probabilistic modes exist in Darts XGBModel.
weaknesses: Same overfitting risk as LightGBM, with no real advantage. Pick one GBM.
evidence: In an IoT vending-machine warehouse (about 1,500 machines), XGBoost reached MAE 22 vs ARIMAX 27, Prophet 37 and SVR 38, and adding exogenous calendar flags helped significantly (Mehmood et al. 2024).

model: CP-SAT scheduling with cumulative / reservoir constraints (OR-Tools)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Later: shifts of production orders or shipments that keep each class's level within capacity over time.
inputs_needed: Order intervals, level changes per event, class capacities.
strengths: Reservoir/cumulative constraints model storage level directly.
weaknesses: Needs plan ownership; semantics of reservoir bounds not confirmed on the pages fetched.
evidence: OR-Tools reference lists Cumulative, CumulativeUsingReservoir and a ReservoirConstraint with AddEvent(time, level_change); the Activimetrics blog uses cumulative constraints for warehouse loading docks.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. OR-Tools reference pages list Cumulative, CumulativeUsingReservoir and ReservoirConstraint.AddEvent(time, level_change); the OR-Tools repo states Apache License 2.0; Activimetrics blog uses a loading-dock cumulative example.

model: Lot-sizing / production-planning MILP with warehouse capacity
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Later: production quantities and timing that respect AW class capacities.
inputs_needed: Demand, setup and holding costs, capacities per period, storage policy.
compute: Seconds to hours depending on size.
strengths: Established models and heuristics exist.
weaknesses: NP-hard when storage allocation is included. Planning ownership sits with Coster planners.
evidence: Minner (2009): savings-based heuristic performed best for multi-product lot sizing with limited warehouse capacity. Iris (2012): the storage allocation policy sets inventory bounds and significantly affects outcomes. IJPE 2004 paper gives an O(T^3) DP for warehouse space and delivery windows.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Later: re-sequencing of moulding/assembly campaigns or shipment dates to level expected AW occupancy and minimise expected shortage per class.
inputs_needed: Plan blocks, pallet output per block, dwell distributions, capacities.
strengths: Mean and variance of occupancy are linear in assignment decisions, so standard MIP works.
weaknesses: Expected shortage is non-linear, so surrogates are used.
evidence: Belien & Demeulemeester: daily bed occupancy is a convolution of block contributions, normal approximation, objective expected bed shortage. Fugener et al. (2014): exact downstream demand distribution for a given schedule. van den Broek d'Obrenan et al.: ILP on expected occupancy scheduled 526 patients in 139 blocks in about 290 s, checked by Monte Carlo.

model: Conformal PID control (quantile tracking + integrator + scorecaster)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Online interval width per class and horizon steered toward target coverage. An optional scorecaster anticipates trends such as month-end.
inputs_needed: Stream of nonconformity scores.
strengths: Deterministic long-run coverage without infinite sets. Generalises ACI.
weaknesses: Hyperparameters (learning rate, integrator). Coverage is long-run only.
evidence: Angelopoulos, Candès & Tibshirani, NeurIPS 2023. Electricity demand: tighter sets than ACI near nominal 90%.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Conformal wrapper around any Darts forecaster (incl. Chronos2Model or regression models) with covariates.
inputs_needed: Pre-trained Darts model plus calibration history.
strengths: Same backtest API as the rest of Darts. Supports whatever covariates the base model does.
weaknesses: Exchangeability assumption.
evidence: Darts README table.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Sequential intervals for fill from bootstrap-ensemble residuals, updated as new snapshots arrive.
inputs_needed: Base regressor plus BlockBootstrap resampling.
strengths: No data splitting. Approximately valid coverage under strongly mixing errors. update() rolls the residual set.
weaknesses: Single-output, so one model is needed per horizon. Coverage is only approximate.
evidence: Xu & Xie, ICML 2021.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Occupancy as arrivals minus departures with an explicit capacity parameter, estimating when a class fills and how many arrivals are turned away to the floor buffer.
inputs_needed: Aggregate occupancy counts; arrival and departure time profiles; capacity.
min_history: A few weeks of aggregate counts.
strengths: Few parameters with operational meaning. Explicit overflow estimate.
weaknesses: Daily profile shape assumptions suit commuters better than production flows.
evidence: Kaltenbrunner et al. (2025): TNL adds a capacity limit; test errors mostly below 4%, 1-hour nowcast median errors 0.18% and 0.08%, and the model without the limit was over 10x worse at a capacity-bound site.

model: Fluid / cumulative-curve approximation (A(t) - D(t) with capacity)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Deterministic build-up and drain of occupancy per class from cumulative planned inflow and outflow curves; time when each class hits capacity and overflow volume to the floor buffer.
inputs_needed: Cumulative planned inflow and outflow per class; capacities.
strengths: Very fast, very explainable 'inventory build-up diagram' for dashboards and quick what-if.
weaknesses: No randomness; diffusion/Monte Carlo refinements needed for bands.
evidence: Technion Service Engineering notes: fluid models replace random processes by rates, work best for predictable variability, and use inventory build-up diagrams for bottlenecks (cranberry example).

model: Real-time micro/macro queue-based probabilistic occupancy prediction
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Probabilistic occupancy forecast at any horizon from current occupants' elapsed durations (micro) or aggregates (macro).
inputs_needed: Arrival and departure timestamps per occupant.
strengths: Reduces forecasting to parameter estimation; provides a lower bound on achievable error.
weaknesses: Assumes queue structure; truck parking has no plans.
evidence: Tavafoghi, Poolla & Varaiya (2019) validate time-varying queue models on 29 truck parking sites (55-299 spots, 16 months) and derive a lower bound on real-time prediction error.

model: SimPy discrete-event model of the AW
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Occupancy per class plus crane, LGV and conveyor workload, I/O queues and defrag mission load under scenarios.
inputs_needed: Flow-balance inputs plus equipment cycle times, LGV fleet size, shift calendars.
min_history: None to build; weeks of data to validate.
strengths: Pure Python, fits the team stack. The allocation cascade and defrag rules become processes, and the same model serves Monte Carlo and what-if.
weaknesses: Equipment-level detail is not needed for daily occupancy, so there is a risk of over-building. No built-in animation.
evidence: PyPI: SimPy 4.1.2 released May 2026, MIT licence, Python 3.8+, process-based discrete-event simulation.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Smoothed level (plus weekly season) of fill per class with Gaussian intervals.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots per class.
min_history: ~3-6 weeks (2+ seasonal cycles for weekly season)
library: statsforecast AutoETS; darts AutoETS / ExponentialSmoothing; statsmodels ETSModel
strengths: Robust, fast and well understood. Analytic intervals. Good univariate challenger to persistence.
weaknesses: Pure ETS has no exogenous inputs. Darts lists future-covariate support for its StatsForecast wrappers, and the StatsForecast signature accepts X, but the docs do not say how X is used. Does not know the plan.
evidence: Darts covariate table marks AutoETS future covariates as supported (wrapper). StatsForecast notes that accepting X in the signature does not guarantee the model uses it.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Extrapolates the recent average daily change in fill per class.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots.
strengths: Picks up the steady fill-up that precedes month-end.
weaknesses: Drift estimated from a short window explodes at a 14-day horizon. Cannot use plans (StatsForecast RandomWalkWithDrift.fit takes only y).
evidence: Listed as a baseline in Darts and StatsForecast.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Autoregressive RNN with parametric likelihood producing sample paths of fill.
inputs_needed: Many related series, covariates.
library: gluonts DeepAREstimator; neuralforecast DeepAR; darts RNNModel (probabilistic = DeepAR-like)
strengths: Sample paths allow path-wise threshold-crossing probability.
weaknesses: Needs far more data than 5 short series.
evidence: NeuralForecast table: DeepAR F/H/S exog supported.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Probabilistic deep models (DeepAR etc.) on PyTorch.
inputs_needed: Dataset with dynamic features.
strengths: Mature probabilistic deep-learning toolkit from AWS.
weaknesses: Data-hungry. AWS effort has largely moved to Chronos and AutoGluon.
evidence: GluonTS GitHub README.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Basis-expansion MLP forecast with exogenous inputs.
inputs_needed: Target plus exog.
strengths: Interpretable trend and seasonality stacks. Exogenous support (NeuralForecast F/H/S).
weaknesses: Data-hungry. Darts NBEATSModel takes no future covariates.
evidence: NeuralForecast table; Olivares et al., IJF 2023.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Multi-rate MLP forecast.
inputs_needed: Target plus exog (NeuralForecast).
strengths: Efficient for long horizons.
weaknesses: Known-future support depends on the library (NeuralForecast yes, Darts no). Data-hungry.
evidence: NeuralForecast and Darts covariate tables.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Deep global models (NHITS, TiDE, TFT, TSMixerx, NBEATSx) with future, historical and static exog.
inputs_needed: df plus futr_exog_list, hist_exog_list, stat_exog_list.
strengths: Clear exog-support matrix per model (F/H/S). Same API family as StatsForecast and MLForecast.
weaknesses: Deep models are data-hungry, and 5 short series are not enough.
evidence: NeuralForecast capability table (e.g. TFT, TiDE, NHITS, NBEATSx, TSMixerx: F/H/S yes; PatchTST: none; TimeXer: H and S only).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Channel-independent patch transformer for long-horizon univariate forecasting.
inputs_needed: Target only.
strengths: Strong on long-horizon benchmark datasets.
weaknesses: No exogenous inputs in NeuralForecast, so it cannot use plans.
evidence: NeuralForecast table: PatchTST has no F/H/S exog.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: All-MLP mixing across time and variates. TSMixerx adds exogenous inputs.
inputs_needed: Multivariate target plus covariates.
library: neuralforecast TSMixer (no exog) / TSMixerx (F/H/S); darts TSMixerModel (all covariates)
strengths: The extended version uses auxiliary information (the paper's M5 experiments).
weaknesses: Data-hungry. Plain TSMixer ignores exog.
evidence: NeuralForecast table; Darts table; Google Research paper.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2303.06053 (TSMixer, auxiliary info, M5), NeuralForecast table (TSMixer none, TSMixerx F/H/S) and Darts table (all covariates, probabilistic; Apache-2.0) match.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Multi-horizon quantiles of fill with static, past and known-future inputs, plus variable-selection weights.
inputs_needed: Static class metadata, past fill, known future plans and calendar.
strengths: Designed exactly for known-future inputs. Attention and variable importance help explanation.
weaknesses: Data-hungry. Below most foundation models in fev-bench.
evidence: fev-bench: TFT probabilistic win rate 51.4% vs Chronos-2 91.4%. NeuralForecast and Darts support F/H/S.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: MLP encoder-decoder forecast using past and known-future covariates.
inputs_needed: Target plus static, past and future covariates.
strengths: Simple, fast, and covariate-native in both libraries. The best deep option if Coster accumulates a year of data.
weaknesses: Still needs much more data than is available now.
evidence: Darts and NeuralForecast tables: past, future and static covariates supported.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Transformer that embeds the endogenous target as patches and exogenous series as variate tokens.
inputs_needed: Target plus exogenous series.
library: neuralforecast TimeXer (H and S exog; no future exog listed); Time-Series-Library
strengths: Purpose-built for exogenous drivers (NeurIPS 2024).
weaknesses: NeuralForecast lists no future-exog support, so the plans would have to be shifted into past features. Data-hungry.
evidence: NeuralForecast table: TimeXer F=no, H=yes, S=yes.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Inverted transformer with attention across variates (could relate the 5 classes).
inputs_needed: Multivariate target, future exog in NeuralForecast.
strengths: Cross-variate attention fits the class-cascade idea.
weaknesses: Data-hungry. No historical or static exog in NeuralForecast.
evidence: NeuralForecast table: iTransformer multivariate, F=yes, H=no, S=no.

model: Siemens Tecnomatix Plant Simulation (High Bay Warehouse library)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Equipment-level twin of the AS/RS for virtual commissioning and stress tests; occupancy as a by-product.
inputs_needed: Rack geometry, crane kinematics, WMS rules, PLC logic.
library: Plant Simulation HBW library (RackLane + WMS objects)
compute: Can run much faster than real time.
strengths: The HBW WMS object tracks free/occupied places and assigns by pallet dimension, a preallocation table, or both, close to Coster's cascade.
weaknesses: Commercial and engineering-heavy. Built for design and commissioning, not daily forecasting.
evidence: Ferrero (Alba, 8,000 pallet spaces, 4 stacker cranes): Plant Simulation twin linked to PLCSIM Advanced cut commissioning time by about 30% (13 vs 19 weeks) and ran up to 50,000x faster than real time.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate quantile forecast of fill per class.
inputs_needed: Context series only.
strengths: Zero-shot. Good univariate probabilistic baseline.
weaknesses: No covariates. Superseded by Chronos-Bolt and Chronos-2.
evidence: Chronos repo: sizes tiny 8M to large 710M. AutoGluon: context 512, prediction 64.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fast zero-shot univariate quantile forecast per class.
inputs_needed: Context series; covariates only via an external regressor in AutoGluon.
strengths: Cheap univariate foundation-model reference that tells whether covariates add value.
weaknesses: No native covariates. The AutoGluon covariate regressor models only per-timestep effects.
evidence: AutoGluon: on electricity load, univariate Bolt-small MASE 1.278 vs Chronos-2 with covariates 0.696. fev-bench probabilistic win rate 67.0%.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Adds past and future covariates to a pretrained univariate model through trained modular adapters.
inputs_needed: Context series plus covariates plus some training data for adapters.
strengths: Shows covariates can be injected without retraining the backbone.
weaknesses: Superseded by native covariate support in Chronos-2. Needs training data Coster lacks.
evidence: Pineda Arango et al. 2025: outperforms baselines on 32 synthetic covariate datasets and on real data.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate probabilistic forecast.
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Ranks 4th in fev-bench.
weaknesses: No covariates in the fev-bench evaluation. Details not verified here.
evidence: fev-bench: probabilistic win rate 73.3%, point 70.5%.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. fev-bench (arXiv 2509.26468v4) ranks FlowState 4th with 73.3% probabilistic and 70.5% point win rate, and notes it ignores covariates.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Univariate probabilistic forecast using lag features.
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Open probabilistic foundation model that fine-tunes well on mid-sized data.
weaknesses: No exogenous covariates. Older. LoRA fine-tuning can degrade short series.
evidence: Rasul et al. 2023. The break-even study (2607.04919) includes Lag-Llama and reports that LoRA fine-tuning can hurt short series.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot any-variate forecast with past and future dynamic features.
inputs_needed: Context series plus dynamic real features.
license: Code Apache-2.0; Salesforce weights research-only (check model card)
strengths: Any-variate attention was an early design for covariates and multivariate input (ICML 2024).
weaknesses: Superseded. Weights carry research-use restrictions.
evidence: Woo et al., ICML 2024 (any-variate attention). Not independently re-verified here.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. PMLR v235 page confirms Moirai (ICML 2024); uni2ts repo is Apache-2.0, release 'for research purposes only', and MoiraiForecast takes feat_dynamic_real and past_feat_dynamic_real.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate quantile forecast per class.
inputs_needed: Context series only.
strengths: Small and fast. Decoder-only with quantile loss.
weaknesses: Univariate only (no cross-variate forecasting). Non-commercial license. fev-bench mid-pack.
evidence: Moirai 2.0 paper: 'designed for univariate time-series input'. fev-bench probabilistic win rate 67.4%.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Generative zero-shot forecast that samples many plausible trajectories (flow-matching TimeFlow loss).
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Raw sample paths allow path-wise threshold-crossing probability.
weaknesses: No covariates mentioned.
evidence: Liu et al. 2025 (pretrained on TimeBench, 1 trillion points).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate point forecast from a sparse mixture-of-experts model (up to 2.4B params).
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Scale research.
weaknesses: No covariates mentioned. Heavy compute. Point forecasts.
evidence: Shi et al., ICLR 2025 (Time-300B pretraining).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Hosted zero-shot forecast with historical exog in df and future exog in X_df.
inputs_needed: df with exog columns plus X_df future exog; API key.
library: nixtla (NixtlaClient.forecast(df, X_df=...)); also Azure AI endpoint
strengths: No infrastructure. Supports future exogenous variables.
weaknesses: Coster's warehouse data would leave the premises. Cost. A closed model that is hard to audit.
evidence: Nixtla docs: future exog via X_df, historical exog in df, models timegpt-1 and timegpt-1-long-horizon.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Zero-shot univariate or multivariate probabilistic forecast, trained mainly on observability data.
inputs_needed: Context series.
strengths: Open weights. Strong on observability (BOOM) data.
weaknesses: Ignores covariates in fev-bench. Pretraining domain far from warehouse stocks.
evidence: fev-bench: Toto-1.0 probabilistic win rate 72.4%. Paper: 151M decoder-only, Apache-2.0.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Coherent forecasts so the 5 class forecasts sum to the total AW fill (and optionally aisles), using the error covariance.
inputs_needed: Base forecasts for every level plus in-sample residuals.
library: hierarchicalforecast (MinTrace; probabilistic: Normality, Bootstrap, PERMBU, Conformal)
strengths: Uses the cross-class error correlation caused by the cascade. Probabilistic reconciliation options.
weaknesses: A small hierarchy (5 to 1) gives modest gains. The total is less important than per-class saturation.
evidence: Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos & Hyndman, JASA 2019.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Daily counts of 'pallets that find no compatible free cell' or floor-buffer overflow events (mostly zero, occasional bursts).
inputs_needed: Daily count series.
library: statsforecast CrostonClassic, TSB, ADIDA, IMAPA; darts Croston
strengths: Designed for sparse counts where ETS and ARIMA fail.
weaknesses: Gives rates, not timing. Better derived from the fill forecast plus capacity logic in the simulator.
evidence: StatsForecast models page (Croston, ADIDA, IMAPA with level and conformal intervals).

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Per-pallet duration of stay at put-away, used for DoS-based slotting; for Coster it could feed per-pallet exit times into the residual-stock model.
inputs_needed: Large movement histories with product and customer features.
min_history: Years of records; the authors released a public cold-storage dataset.
strengths: Shows DoS can be predicted at scale in a cold-storage network and pays off operationally.
weaknesses: Far too data hungry for a few months of post-change history. Unnecessary where plans already give exit times for most pallets.
evidence: ICLR 2020 poster: ParallelNet reached 29% MAPE on DoS (about 30% better than CNN-LSTM), degraded less over time, and warehouse pilots reported up to 19-21% labour savings.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Dwell-time bucket (e.g., <2 d, 2-7 d, 1-4 weeks, >4 weeks) for pallets without an exit plan.
inputs_needed: Material, customer, arrival weekday and day of month, destination.
strengths: Ordinal treatment respects bucket order and works on small data.
weaknesses: When exits depend on outside parties, accuracy can be very low (best exact-class accuracy about 7% at Arica). Buckets are too coarse for a 48 h alert.
evidence: De Armas Jacomino et al. (2021): ordinal regression had the lowest MAE in 15 of 21 experiments (71%). Gaete et al. (2017): low classification accuracy, yet dwell-class segregation cut rehandles by about 17% in Jan-Apr 2012.

model: Random survival forest / gradient-boosted survival models
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Individual pallet survival curves with non-linear covariate effects, feeding the residual-stock model.
inputs_needed: As Cox model plus richer features (order status, position in plan, customer history).
strengths: Captures interactions. scikit-learn style API with censored-data metrics.
weaknesses: GPL-3 matters if embedded in a distributed product. Data hungry. Better individual accuracy may not improve aggregate occupancy.
evidence: Poelsterl (2020) lists Random Survival Forest, penalized Cox and survival SVM in scikit-survival; its API also provides GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis and ComponentwiseGradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis. Hartwig et al. (2024) find that occupancy accuracy depends more on the symmetry of LOS prediction errors than on their size.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. scikit-survival is GPL-3 with RSF, penalized Cox and survival SVM (JMLR) and its API also has GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis; Hartwig et al. (HEALTHINF 2024) abstract confirms error symmetry matters more than error size.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Interval from quantile regression (e.g. QRF) on recent residuals, exploiting their autocorrelation.
inputs_needed: Residual history.
strengths: Narrower intervals than other conformal methods when residuals are autocorrelated.
weaknesses: Needs a longer residual history than Coster has now. Asymptotic guarantee only.
evidence: Xu & Xie, ICML 2023.

model: AnyLogic (multi-method DES / agent-based, Material Handling Library)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Detailed AW and LGV model for what-if studies; can forecast KPIs from Excel inputs.
inputs_needed: Inventory state, inbound and outbound data, product/pallet matrix, layout.
strengths: Storage element with storage policies, Store/Retrieve/Storage System blocks, AGV transporters with collision handling and routing API, conveyors, cranes.
weaknesses: Commercial licence and Java tooling outside the team's Python stack. Heavy for a daily forecast.
evidence: AnyLogic case study (Western Digital/DSV warehouse in Thailand, built by EPIC InnoLabs): forecasting simulation with Excel inputs (inventory state, inbound, outbound, product matrix), 3-month horizon planned to grow to 7 months; no quantitative results yet.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Queueing-network view of pallets moving palletiser -> AW -> assembly -> AW, with blocking.
inputs_needed: Arrival and service distributions per node, routing matrix.
license: not stated on PyPI page (see GitHub)
strengths: Focus on reproducibility. Type I blocking, baulking, server schedules, customer classes, deadlock detection.
weaknesses: The queueing abstraction does not natively represent heterogeneous cell sizes or a cascade, so it fits the AW poorly.
evidence: Palmer et al. (2017) arXiv describe Ciw and benchmark it against other DES frameworks; PyPI lists blocking, baulking and server schedules.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: 3D DES of racks, docks, conveyors and AGVs for layout and resource what-if.
inputs_needed: Layout, equipment parameters, order profiles.
strengths: Prebuilt racks, docks, conveyors, AGVs and labour objects; true-to-scale 3D.
weaknesses: Commercial; the vendor page gives no customer results; not aimed at daily forecasting.
evidence: Autodesk warehouse-simulation page describes a DES engine with prepackaged storage systems and AGV modules.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Generic process DES of the AW for what-if.
inputs_needed: Process flow, distributions.
strengths: Long-established in teaching and industry.
weaknesses: Commercial, Windows-only, not integrated with a Python pipeline; no clear advantage for this problem.
evidence: Rockwell press release (July 2013) on Arena 14.5 extending 3-D animation to conveyors and transporters; it gives no licensing or platform details beyond a .NET-based Visual Designer.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. The cited page is a July 2013 Rockwell press release on Arena 14.5 3-D animation for conveyors/transporters; it says nothing about licensing, and only mentions the .NET-based Visual Designer.

model: Short-term process simulation from reconstructed current state (process mining)
what_it_predicts_for_coster: Reconstructs the in-flight state from a partial event log to start a short-term simulation without warm-up; relevant because Coster's movement log is hard to use.
inputs_needed: Event log of ongoing cases.
strengths: Shows how to infer current state when no clean snapshot exists.
weaknesses: Research-stage; Coster has a daily snapshot, so mostly a fallback.
evidence: Avramenko (2025) reconstructs state from partial logs; on real logs it matched workload exactly and was comparable on timing, except BPIC17.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Same scope as the SimPy model, with 2D/3D animation for showing the AW and LGVs to stakeholders.
inputs_needed: As SimPy model.
strengths: Built-in components, queues, resources, stores, states and monitors. No yield statements needed. Works with Python in Excel.
weaknesses: Smaller community than SimPy. Animation is a nice-to-have, not a forecasting need.
evidence: JOSS paper (van der Ham 2018); PyPI lists version 26.0.8 (June 2026), MIT licence, 2D/3D animation and monitors.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Joint linear state-space forecast of the 5 class fill series, using future covariates.
inputs_needed: Multivariate daily snapshots plus plan covariates.
strengths: Multivariate, so it can learn cross-class spill-over from the cascade. Accepts future covariates.
weaknesses: Identified state dimension is a black box. Small data makes N4SID unstable.
evidence: Darts table: KalmanForecaster supports multivariate, probabilistic output and future covariates.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fill per class as trend + weekday seasonality + plan regressors + Italian holidays and plant shutdowns.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots, future regressor values, holiday table.
min_history: several months (1+ year for yearly seasonality)
strengths: Easy to explain. Since v1.4, predict_spec fits nested models for regressors that are not fully known and avoids leakage in cross-validation.
weaknesses: Trend extrapolation is fragile on short, regime-shifted series. The additive linear form cannot represent saturation. Often beaten by simple methods.
evidence: Prophet docs: regressors must be known for history and future. Enfint's warehouse stock-volume case found SARIMA better than Prophet, TBATS and LSTM.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Fill per class with multiple seasonalities (weekly plus monthly cycle).
inputs_needed: Long daily history.
strengths: Handles complex and non-integer seasonality (De Livera et al. 2011).
weaknesses: Overkill for a few months of data. StatsForecast AutoTBATS ignores X and has no conformal option.
evidence: StatsForecast models page: AutoTBATS ignores X. JASA 2011 paper.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Univariate fill trajectory per class, using theta-line decomposition.
inputs_needed: Daily snapshots.
strengths: A strong univariate method in M-competitions, and cheap.
weaknesses: Darts Theta has no covariates. StatsForecast AutoTheta accepts X in its signature, but use is undocumented. Not designed for bounded stock series.
evidence: Darts table: Theta has no covariates. StatsForecast lists AutoTheta with level and conformal intervals.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Joint dynamics of the 5 class fill ratios (cascade spill-over), with exogenous plan terms.
inputs_needed: Multivariate daily snapshots plus exog.
min_history: 100+ obs (5 series x p lags parameters)
strengths: Explicit cross-class effects. Impulse responses can show how filling Medium pushes into High.
weaknesses: Parameter count grows fast. Assumes stationarity (statsmodels warns), so differencing is needed. Unreliable with a few months of data.
evidence: statsmodels VAR docs; Darts table: VARIMA multivariate with future covariates.

what_it_predicts_for_coster: Aggregate AW + floor-buffer stocks with feedback from weekly entry caps and month-end build-up, for long-term capacity policy.
inputs_needed: Aggregate flows, policy rules.
strengths: Good for policy feedback questions (cap rules, overflow re-entry, month-end).
weaknesses: Aggregates away cell classes and discrete pallets. Adds nothing over the flow balance at a 1-14 day horizon.
evidence: Rodrigues et al. (2011) used system dynamics to identify an optimum warehouse capacity; Sterman's Business Dynamics is the standard text.
